official_sources.title: OGC JSON-FG valid geometry requirement
official_sources.finding: JSON-FG requires Point, LineString, Polygon, Multi-geometry and GeometryCollection members to be valid according to Simple Feature Access, including embedded geometries.
official_sources.limitation: Conformance establishes structural validity, not cadastral positional accuracy or preservation of legal parcel meaning after repair.

official_sources.title: GDAL geometry validity and scope limitations
official_sources.finding: GDAL warns that invalid geometries can produce incorrect intersection results; individual validity checks do not detect inter-feature gaps or overlaps, and spikes or slivers are outside validity scope.
official_sources.limitation: A geometry passing IsValid still requires layer-level coverage and qualitative change checks.

official_sources.title: GDAL check-geometry error location and curve caveat
official_sources.finding: The checker reports invalidity descriptions and usually an error point; polygon validity and line simplicity are GEOS-backed, while curved geometries are linearized and can change validity outcomes.
official_sources.limitation: One reported point may not enumerate every defect, and linearized curves require separate provenance.

official_sources.title: GDAL polygon coverage validity
official_sources.finding: A valid polygon coverage has no overlaps, shared edges node at the same locations, and no gaps below the configured width; invalid edges are emitted for inspection.
official_sources.limitation: Coverage validity is layer-level and must not silently alter legal parcel ownership to close defects.

official_sources.title: OGRGeometry validity, repair and precision API
official_sources.finding: OGRGeometry exposes IsValid, MakeValid and SetPrecision; predicates do not validate inputs, MakeValid can return lower-dimensional or multi-geometries, and SetPrecision rounds to a grid while preserving validity.
official_sources.limitation: Repair can change type, component count, winding or dimensionality and therefore requires explicit before/after acceptance metrics.

official_sources.title: ogr2ogr make-valid, coordinate precision and simplification order
official_sources.finding: ogr2ogr make-valid removes lower-dimensional subgeometries after repair; coordinate resolution can trigger SetPrecision, while simplify preserves topology per feature but not necessarily across a whole layer and segmentize runs before reprojection.
official_sources.limitation: Per-feature validity is not proof that adjacent parcels still share identical edges after processing.

official_sources.title: GEOS MakeValid dimensional and multipart outcomes
official_sources.finding: GEOS MakeValid attempts to retain input vertices, but self-intersecting polygons may become multipolygons and dimensional collapses may produce lower-dimensional geometries or collections.
official_sources.limitation: Vertex retention alone does not guarantee equivalent parcel area, holes, connectivity or legal identity.

official_sources.title: GEOS OverlayNG explicit precision robustness
official_sources.finding: OverlayNG accepts an explicit precision model; fixed precision uses snap rounding for robust valid output, whereas floating precision is not fully robust and can raise TopologyException.
official_sources.limitation: The grid size must be justified from source coordinate precision and parcel scale; an arbitrary coarse grid can erase narrow legitimate features.
